belief: The people who disagree with me are evil.
origins: Constant exposure to outrage, friends who share one view, and media that profits from anger teach us to see the other side as enemies. Friendships and families fracture. We feel righteous but also anxious and angry.
teaches: Jesus said, “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.” Paul writes, “Our struggle is not against flesh and blood,” and “Do not repay anyone evil for evil… If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.” “A gentle answer turns away wrath.” James says, “Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger.” Proverbs warns, “He who answers a matter before he hears it—this is folly and disgrace to him.” We can hold convictions firmly and still treat those who differ as people made in God’s image.
self_statements: They want to destroy the country.
Anyone who thinks that is a bad person.
There is no good in them.
I cannot be friends with them.
errors: Seeing people as completely good or evil.
Feeling angry and concluding that they are wicked.
questions: What do I actually know about the people who disagree with me?
Do I know anyone personally with a different view, and are they evil?
What does Jesus say about enemies?
How is my anger affecting me?
What are my own blind spots?
How can I listen before I answer?
truth: People who disagree with me are made in God’s image, not enemies to destroy. I can hold convictions firmly, listen well, and speak with gentleness. My struggle is not against flesh and blood.
hw_truths: I am called to love my enemies.
My struggle is not against flesh and blood.
A gentle answer turns away wrath.
I can be quick to listen.
Peace is possible where I can.
Others are made in God’s image.
log: Each week, note one conversation where you listened before answering.
actions: Notice how much outrage media you consume.
Ask someone with a different view to explain why.
Pray for the person or group you resent.
Use it when you feel heated.
prayer: Lord, I have judged those who disagree with me. Soften my heart, teach me to listen, and help me love my enemies as You command. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “I will love my enemies and pray for them.”
